subject: Request for subprocessor encryption matrix and vendor mapping for SOC2/transfer review
messages:
From: Sana Patel <sana.patel@fincloud.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: security-ops@fincloud.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor & encryption matrix for upcoming SOC2 review

Hi Kimberly,

We are preparing for our external SOC2 audit next quarter and our audit team has asked for a detailed inventory of Redwood's subprocessors along with an encryption mapping (at-rest / in-transit) per subprocessor. Specifically, they want: 

- Full list of subprocessors used in production for inference and logging
- Which data classes are processed by each subprocessor (tokens, metadata, logs)
- Encryption at-rest and in-transit controls per vendor (algorithms, key management where applicable)
- Any recent changes to the roster in the last 12 months and effective dates
- Evidence artifacts if available (attestations or certs)

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide this matrix and an ETA? Our scope is EU customer data first, but the auditor may request global transfer paths.

Thanks,
Sana Patel
Information Security Manager, FinCloud Inc.
security: +1 415-555-0133

Hi Sana — thanks for the heads up and the clear checklist. We can produce the requested matrix and supporting artifacts. Quick clarifying questions before we compile everything: 

- Confirming scope: you said EU customer data first — do you want EU-only processors (for SCC/residency mapping) or a global list as well?
- Do you need an explicit column for applicable legal basis (e.g., SCCs, adequacy) or is transfer path + encryption controls sufficient?

I will loop in Marissa (customer success) to coordinate delivery and Jordan (legal) for any contractual notes. We'll aim to get an initial package within 3 business days if EU-only; global export will take ~7 business days.

If you can confirm scope by EOD today, we'll prioritize.

Best,
Kimberly Park
